text:
anna: FYI I threw together a quick prototype for 'opaque route pruning' to keep the policy graph from exploding when tenants add lots of ephemeral routes. gist: prune nodes that are unreachable for X epochs and collapse equivalent leaves.

josh: Can you sketch the invariants we need to preserve? my main worry is cache key stability + tie-breaking when prunes reintroduce previously pruned routes. :thinking:

anna: good point. proto rules I used: 1) only prune nodes with no observed hits for N windows, 2) when pruning we emit a stable placeholder ID so downstream resolvers can detect rehydration, 3) we keep a tombstone with last-seen-routing-hash for compatibility.

kiran: how does this affect the runtime adapters? if the adapter expects route ids to be stable, placeholder IDs could cause churn.

anna: adapters should treat placeholder ids as opaque but stable until rehydrated. idea: placeholder format = `prune:<original-hash>:v<version>` so adapters can ignore or special-case.

marco: can we avoid changing adapter contracts? any change that requires adapter updates will slow rollouts.

anna: plan A avoids adapter changes: we keep original ids in a shadow map in the controller and only hand adapters the same ids when we guarantee live routing. when pruned we hand them the placeholder but also advertise a `compat:legacy-id` header in the mapping api. adapters can ignore it.

josh: ok but that means more state in controller. what's the memory/cost tradeoff?

anna: prototype shows ~3% memory increase for 10k low-traffic routes, with 40% reduction in eval traversal time under heavy policy churn. numbers are sketchy but promising.

kiran: rollout strategy? I want canary, metrics, and automatic rollback if request error rate climbs.

anna: proposed rollout: feature-flag gated, enable prune-only (no tombstones) in a small canary, after 48h switch to tombstones, then enable placeholder ids. Metrics to watch: route-miss-rate, adapter-id-churn, policy-eval-latency, tail-99 latency.

marco: add a safety: if a pruned route gets >M hits within T seconds we instant-rehydrate and emit a `rehydrated` event to the audit log.

anna: already in proto: rehydrate window + backoff. event emits to ops and to tenant audit stream.

josh: compatibility with rollbacks across versions? if old control plane talks to new router or vice-versa we need graceful fallback.

anna: compatibility matrix: new controller <-> old adapter => placeholder ids shown, adapters ignore placeholder and keep serving last-known mapping. old controller <-> new adapter => adapter treats unknown ids as miss and falls back to default route; we plan a sticky fallback behavior for 7 days to avoid oscillation.

kiran: can we add a short-lived lease on placeholders so adapters don't persist them indefinitely?

anna: yes, placeholder TTL = 7d by default; config per-tenant.

sre-bot: deploybot: canary deployment scheduled to infra-canary cluster at 2026-03-21T22:00Z.

marco: one more ask: add a small deterministic checksum in mapping API so both controller and adapter can quickly detect mismatch and trigger reconciliation instead of full diff.

anna: will add `mapping-checksum` header to the mapping API and controller reconciliation logs.

josh: sounds reasonable. next steps: anna to update RFC with the new compatibility matrix + rollout checklist, kiran to draft monitoring and alert rules, marco to review adapter read path changes for no-contract updates.

anna: thanks. I'll post a short RFC update by EOD with code snippets and the proto link. :thumbsup:

marco: :+1:

kiran: thanks, looking forward to the alert drafts.

sre-bot: incidentbot: reminder - add runbook entries for rehydration incidents.
